items.title: Funza Lushaka Bursary: returning bursars
items.elig: Current Funza Lushaka bursars who need funding for 2027. You must reapply every year.
items.get: Teaching-degree costs for another year. You teach one year in a public school for each year funded.
items.step: Log in at eservices.gov.za and complete the re-application before 30 November.
items.note: New applicants have until 31 January 2027 (see the next listing).

items.title: Funza Lushaka Bursary: new applicants
items.elig: South Africans studying or planning to study a BEd or PGCE at a public university, in priority teaching subjects.
items.get: Full bursary for teacher training. You teach one year in a public school for each year funded.
items.step: Apply for university admission first, then apply online at eservices.gov.za.

items.title: Emfuleni Mayoral Bursary 2027
items.by: Emfuleni Local Municipality (Vanderbijlpark, Vereeniging, Sebokeng, Evaton, Sharpeville)
items.elig: Grade 12 learners living in Emfuleni, starting first-year full-time study in 2027. Proof of address is needed, such as a certified municipal bill.
items.get: Tuition, books and a laptop. Accommodation and meals for selected students only.
items.step: Collect a form at a municipal office or public library (07:45 to 16:15) or download it from the municipal website. Enquiries: 084 686 4418.
items.note: Reported by education news sites that cite the municipality’s announcement and contacts. Confirm the form on the municipal website.

items.title: NYDA Grant Programme
items.elig: South African citizens aged 18 to 35 with a youth-owned business or co-operative, from idea stage to growth.
items.get: Non-repayable grants from R1 000 to R200 000 (up to R250 000 in total for agriculture and technology co-operatives), plus mentorship.
items.needs: ID, business plan, CIPC registration for formal businesses, a two-year commitment to NYDA mentorship.
items.step: Register on the NYDA online portal or visit a branch. Call centre: 0800 52 52 52.

items.title: NYDA Voucher Programme
items.get: Business services worth R6 600 to R19 800 from an NYDA-accredited provider, such as bookkeeping, a business plan or marketing.
items.step: Ask for the voucher programme when you register on the NYDA portal or at a branch.

items.title: SAYouth: jobs, learnerships and youth employment programmes
items.elig: South Africans aged 18 to 34 who are not working or studying.
items.get: One profile that matches you to entry-level jobs and learnerships. Government school-assistant programmes recruit only through this platform.
items.step: Go to sayouth.mobi (free of data on major networks), register with your ID and cell number and complete your profile in full. Helpline: 0800 727 272.
items.note: The next phase of the Basic Education Employment Initiative had not been announced when we last checked. Ignore posts that say it is open unless they link to sayouth.mobi.

items.title: SEDFA small business finance and support
items.by: Small Enterprise Development and Finance Agency (formerly SEFA and SEDA)
items.elig: South African-owned small businesses and co-operatives, usually registered with CIPC.
items.get: Loans, credit guarantees, some blended finance with a grant portion, and free business development support. Most finance must be repaid.
items.needs: CIPC registration, tax compliance, bank statements, a business plan.
items.step: Start with business development support at a SEDFA branch to strengthen your application, then apply on the SEDFA website.

items.title: Spaza Shop Support Fund
items.by: Department of Small Business Development, through SEDFA and the National Empowerment Fund
items.elig: South African-owned spaza shops and township retailers.
items.get: Stock, equipment and compliance support through a R500 million fund that combines grants and concessional loans.
items.needs: South African ownership, a trading permit or business licence, CIPC registration. Licensing has been the main reason applications stall.
items.step: Sort out your trading licence with your municipality first, then apply through SEDFA or the NEF.

items.title: Government tenders: eTender Portal and Central Supplier Database
items.elig: Registered businesses, NPOs and co-operatives. Small and youth-owned firms can bid, but must meet compliance rules.
items.get: Contracts to supply goods and services to national, provincial and municipal government and state-owned entities.
items.needs: Central Supplier Database (CSD) registration, valid tax compliance status, B-BBEE certificate or affidavit, CIDB grading for construction work.
items.step: Register on the CSD first; it is free. Then filter the eTender Portal by province and category, and check your municipality’s supply chain notices for smaller quotations.
items.note: Most small contracts are quotations under R1 million advertised by municipalities and provincial departments, not national tenders.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master’s scholarships
items.elig: Graduates of any nationality with a bachelor’s degree. Each programme sets its own requirements.
items.get: Full scholarship for a two-year master’s across several European universities: fees, travel and a monthly allowance of about €1 400.
items.closeText: Most close between December 2026 and February 2027
items.step: Browse the official catalogue, shortlist up to three programmes and check each programme’s own deadline.
items.note: There is no single deadline; each programme sets its own. The date shown is typical.

items.title: Stipendium Hungaricum 2027/28
items.by: Government of Hungary, administered by Tempus Public Foundation
items.elig: Citizens of partner countries applying for bachelor’s, master’s or PhD study in Hungary.
items.get: Free tuition, a monthly stipend, an accommodation contribution and medical insurance.
items.step: Watch stipendiumhungaricum.hu for the 2027/28 call. Check that South Africa is on the partner list and which body nominates South African applicants.
items.note: The 2027/28 call had not been published when we last checked. Dates are based on previous years.

items.title: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları) 2027
items.elig: International students: under 21 for bachelor’s, under 30 for master’s, under 35 for PhD.
items.get: University placement, tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, flights, health insurance and a one-year Turkish language course.
items.step: Prepare transcripts and a statement of purpose now. Apply only on turkiyeburslari.gov.tr; no agents are authorised to apply for you.
items.note: Dates follow the official annual calendar; the 2027 notice is usually posted in late December.

items.title: NSFAS bursary
items.elig: South Africans from households earning R350 000 or less a year, at public universities and TVET colleges.
items.get: Tuition, accommodation, transport and learning materials.
items.next: The 2027 cycle closed on 31 October 2026 with no extension. The next cycle has opened in September in recent years.
items.step: Gather ID, household income proof and the consent form before the next window opens.

items.title: Chevening Scholarships
items.by: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
items.elig: Graduates with at least two years’ work experience from eligible countries, including South Africa.
items.get: Fully funded one-year master’s in the UK: fees, living allowance and flights.
items.next: The 2027/28 round closed on 6 October 2026. The next round is expected to open in August 2027.
items.step: Use the year to choose three UK courses and draft your four essays.

items.title: Mandela Washington Fellowship
items.elig: Young African leaders aged 25 to 35 (exceptional applicants from 21) living in eligible countries.
items.get: Six-week fully funded leadership institute at a US university.
items.next: The 2027 round closed on 13 October 2026. Recent rounds have opened in September.
items.step: Build a record of community or business leadership you can describe with results.
